description:
Redwood Inference is expanding enterprise security posture for Hosted, Dedicated, and (especially) Private deployments. This project standardizes the audit log event schema and reaches 100% coverage for sensitive actions across the platform so customers (and internal security/compliance) can reliably: (1) detect and investigate suspicious behavior, (2) satisfy SOC 2/ISO-aligned controls, and (3) export events to SIEMs with consistent semantics.

Goals
- Define a single canonical audit event schema (versioned) with required fields, consistent actor/target semantics, and explicit event taxonomy.
- Achieve 100% coverage for “sensitive actions” across API, Console/admin, control plane, routing/policy changes, RBAC changes, credential lifecycle, data retention/config, Private install/upgrade operations, and audit log export configuration.
- Provide a compatibility strategy (schema versioning + migration/normalization) so customers can consume logs across releases without breaking.
- Add enforcement and verification: build-time linting for event emission, runtime/telemetry-based coverage dashboards, and regression tests.
- Improve operability: runbooks for audit pipeline outages, backfill strategy, retention/redaction rules, and SIEM export guidance.

Scope
- In-scope systems: API Gateway, Control Plane services (tenant/config/policy/RBAC), Console backend/admin actions, Private installer/upgrade tooling, audit-log-exporter, observability ingestion, and data residency/retention configuration surfaces.
- In-scope outputs: Confluence standards + ADRs, implementation PRs, Linear project plan, Slack coordination, customer-facing support artifacts (Jira), and sales/security review collateral (Gmail/Fireflies/HubSpot).
- Out-of-scope: building a full customer-facing “audit log UI” beyond basic viewing/export configuration; new compliance certifications (this project supports them but is not itself the audit).

Key stakeholders / owners
- Product: Naomi Feldman (Security & Compliance), Vivek Kulkarni (Private Deployments), Marissa Cole / Paula Mendes (Console & Rollouts dependencies).
- Security Engineering: Marcus Lin (exec owner for engineering delivery), Kevin Osei (audit log export + SIEM), Hanae Suzuki (supporting security eng).
- Platform/Engineering: Ethan Park (control plane), Priya Natarajan (platform org sponsor), Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman (telemetry), Allison Grant (observability standards), Neha Kapoor / Sean Gallagher (SRE for reliability + incident response).
- GRC: Olga Petrov (control mapping, evidence expectations).

Timeline (hypothetical)
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): inventory current events, define “sensitive actions” list, gap analysis by service.
- Phase 1 (2–4 weeks): schema design + ADRs + reference implementation library; define versioning/backcompat policy.
- Phase 2 (4–8 weeks): roll out instrumentation service-by-service; add CI enforcement + tests.
- Phase 3 (2–4 weeks): coverage verification (dashboards + sampling), operational runbooks, customer export guidance, and launch comms.

Constraints / non-functional requirements
- Minimize PII: explicitly classify fields, enforce redaction/hashing rules, and avoid logging secrets.
- Cardinality control: constrain free-form strings, enumerate action types, and cap dimensions.
- Multi-deployment consistency: Hosted/Dedicated/Private must emit equivalent events for equivalent actions.
- Reliability: audit pipeline must be resilient (buffering/retry), with clear failure modes and on-call guidance.

Deliverables
- Canonical schema v1 (JSON schema + field dictionary) + event taxonomy for sensitive actions.
- Implementation library + service integration checklist.
- Coverage dashboard and “missing events” alerts.
- SIEM export format guidance + customer-facing security FAQ updates.
- Evidence mapping notes for SOC2/ISO controls and audit readiness.
